Hearthstone Hospice Inpatient Unit - DISCHARGE SUMMARY Name: GEBREYES, ALMAZ MRN: 0612-884 DOB: 04/17/2006 Admission: 09/20/2082 Discharge: 10/01/2082 Attending: Fitzgerald Obuya, MD
This 76 y.o. woman with end stage chronic obstructive bronchitis, ischaemic heart disease, diabetic kidney disease stage 3 and a previously treated breast cancer was admitted from home for symptom control of breathlessness and anxiety, following hospice intake on 09/10/2082. Over the twelve days of the stay her dyspnoea was managed with positioning, a fan, low flow oxygen and comfort medications as per the unit protocol, her anxiety settled, and the family were taught how to give them. Pain scores stayed at 0 to 2. Appetite poor. Weight not repeated. Last creatinine 2.0, not repeated.
Hospital course by problem: 1. Respiratory - as above. No need for escalation. Goals of care reviewed, DNR/DNI in place, the form is signed by Dr. Mokoena and the patient's thumbprint, witnessed by her daughter Rahel and the chaplain Fr. Anselm Teague. 2. Cardiac - metoprolol continued while she could swallow, clopidogrel stopped on 09/24, simvastatin stopped. Nitroglycerin spray at bedside. 3. Renal - no changes. Fluids by mouth as desired. 4. Psychosocial - her husband Tekle Mehari, age 92 by now (he had a birthday on 9/27), stayed overnight in the family room most nights; their son Daniel flew in from Seattle on Sept. 28th. Neighbour Mrs. Vance-Brody brought injera and coffee for the family.
Condition at discharge: weak but comfortable, alert for part of the day, oriented. Discharged home with hospice nursing visits at 1840 Delmar Blvd apt 6C and a hospital bed delivered by the vendor, Sunday - sorry, Thursday 10/01/2082.
Medications at discharge: metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily (held if SBP < 100), nitroglycerin spray PRN, comfort kit in the fridge. (The pasted med list below is from 07/09/2082 and is out of date.)
>>> Pasted from 07/09/2082 urgent care note: Pt Almaz Gebreyes 76 y/o F, c/o cough x 3d. BP 108/86, wt 70.3 kg, BMI 29.3. Creat 2.0 eGFR 33. Meds: clopidogrel, simvastatin 10 + 20 (dupe), metoprolol succ, NTG spray. Seen by Bao Nguyen-Park, PA-C. Signed 7/9/82 18:40.
Follow up: hospice RN visits twice weekly and PRN, on call 1-800-555-0123. Dictated but not read. Dictated by Fitzgerald Obuya 10/01/2082 17:30; typed 10/02/2082.
